checkpoints.top_reasoning: No murder or concrete evidence yet. Tess has a family relationship to the donor; Vincent signals objections to his early work; Brie resents donor instructions; these are slight potential motives only. Hugh, Elon and Penny suggest financial or ownership conflict. None warrants a meaningful lead.
checkpoints.naturalness: Introductions have distinct occupational voices and several effective jokes, though nearly everyone delivers the same compact name-role-witty-warning format. Enough personality for an ensemble, little individual depth yet.

checkpoints.top_reasoning: Artie faces forced resignation, the sharpest explicit personal motive. Brie and service staff have access to a private toast and a custom glass; Chip and Cary plausibly handle the labeled poison bottle. Barb and Minnie connect to the deliberately false equipment-fault privacy entry. The inert-liquid lender claim may conceal real poison, but no actual murder method is established. Educational cuts and ownership disputes distribute motives widely.
checkpoints.naturalness: Clues coherently interlock donor control, ownership and service, rather than random secrets. Heavy use of draft/not accepted/withheld qualifications is a little conspicuous and leaves most conflicts hypothetical. Many clues feel carefully written to neutralize one tempting inference immediately.

checkpoints.top_reasoning: Death follows the private toast, raising Brie because food/drink service is now directly relevant. Artie's proposed removal remains a strong anticipatory motive, even unsigned. Poisoning is plausible given the bottle, but sequence alone cannot identify cause or poison delivery. The other scores remain unchanged because the notice adds no personal opportunity evidence.
checkpoints.naturalness: A restrained discovery beat, but administrative gift-status caveats dominate what could be an emotionally sharp death announcement. Repeating that these terms were unaccepted feels procedural rather than like shocked people responding.

checkpoints.top_reasoning: Artie's livelihood and Hugh's firm face the clearest severe losses. Hugh admits falsifying his file and a demand for career-ending admission tonight. Brie, Cary, Barb and Minnie remain important for physical/service access or privacy, but their financial/professional threats alone do not single them out. Grant blackmails or appropriates so many people that almost every motive is credible but nondiscriminating. No account yet establishes the lethal step.
checkpoints.naturalness: Voices remain recognizable: Monet wages, Hugh certificate versus refund, Anne school buses, Faye camera originals. However almost every speech repeats Grant wanted X, I had compromised Y, I resisted Z, ending in a polished aphorism. Thirty conveniently simultaneous coercive disputes strain plausibility and produce an overly uniform defensive rhythm. Characters sound unusually candid about their own misconduct while uniformly witty after a death.

checkpoints.top_reasoning: Poison is localized to a glass left unattended 6:32–7:04, with shared punch/food clean. That weakens generalized catering contamination and strengthens a deliberate individual-glass attack. Chip and Cary have plausible bottle/cupboard handling access; Brie can approach glass or service infrastructure. Artie retains motive and museum access, Hugh's access is less established. The split rear band indicates concealment, but no named person is tied to it. Service manager is not one of the suspects and identity should not be merged with Brie.
checkpoints.naturalness: Timeline is clear and changes the deduction usefully. The extra-course ticket explanation is believable bureaucracy, although its careful separation from the paid toast sounds like an answer to an anticipated rules dispute. Cyanide persisting in an 1891 evidence bottle is an unusual premise accepted as the supplied lab fact.

checkpoints.top_reasoning: Brie now admits going to the unattended place with flavoring intended for that drink, providing the most direct liquid-to-glass opportunity. Her statement labels it culinary but no verification appears yet. Anya directly accesses the cupboard containing the bottle with her spare key; Chip created the split-capable band. Tess, Dada, Barb and Minnie all admit contact with the set place/private room, a meaningful opportunity cluster. Hugh knowingly concealed conflicting contents descriptions. I cannot yet connect any one suspect to both active poison and glass strongly enough to call it obvious.
checkpoints.naturalness: Acts integrate useful admissions and revised behavior, but the same structure recurs across the ensemble: I removed/revised/withdrew a document, here is my embarrassing error, here is a limiting explanation. The bottle preview suddenly acquires a very large attendance list. Brie's flavoring stands out because it is unusually direct physical action among repetitive paperwork confessions; this may make her conspicuous even if innocent. Distinct vocabulary survives the common structure.

checkpoints.top_reasoning: Chip, Anya and Brie remain joint leaders: treatment-band access, direct poison-cupboard access, and direct glass flavoring respectively. Clean retained flavoring verifies an innocent component but does not rule out a separate poison addition during Brie's visit. Ordinary staff keys remove Anya's exclusive-access advantage. Full staff warning means several insiders could know contents were hazardous, including Art E. Fact and Reed. Paige and Robin were actually in the private room with the prepared glass despite earlier emphasis on the public interview. Tess's succession motive weakens because acceptance never occurred. Artie has explicitly forgone the gift, lowering urgency. Corrections and settlements weaken some motives without proving innocence.
checkpoints.naturalness: Exhibits support physical distinctions clearly, especially bottle versus wooden model, clean flavoring, and powered-off camera. Yet this stage reads like a large adjudication packet: nearly every confession gets a corrective receipt, refund or withdrawal. The shared moral-repair arc feels mechanical. The paper scrap lacks a unique match, making it useful for poison-source inference but weak for identity. Exact times for suspect movement remain absent, so confident elimination would overreach.

checkpoints.top_reasoning: Hugh becomes the strong leading culprit: he introduces a claimed canceled original-contents condition and inert substitution that directly contradict the seller's fulfillment statement (no cancellation/substitution instruction received), retained original contents and cyanide lab results. His prior role arranging the purchase and withholding the seller account gives him informed involvement. Everyone else substantially aligns their final explanation with documentary evidence; Hugh alone invents an unsupported delivery change. This identifies a highly suspicious lie, not an independently proved hand-to-glass timeline. Brie, Anya, Chip and Barb remain physical-opportunity alternatives at 6; they could commit the act while Hugh lies to conceal commercial liability.
checkpoints.naturalness: Hugh's late factual contradiction is striking and easy to detect beside the seller document. His 'Stop treating two purchases as one transaction' defense is plausible bluster, but sits awkwardly alongside an explicit claim disproved by a supplied receipt. Other final speeches mostly retell the exhibits with admissions, regrets and corrected paperwork. That creates a readable puzzle-resolution exercise but very little new interpersonal movement. Grant's death rarely disrupts the uniformly polished voices beyond an occasional pointed reference.

final_feedback: Strongest suspect: Hugh Bidder, 9/10. First obvious-candidate stage is 8; no earlier checkpoint singled one person out convincingly. His canceled-condition/inert-substitution claim contradicts the seller's explicit no-cancellation fulfillment, original-content purchase and actual poison. This is a persuasive identity signal by elimination of explanations, but it does not itself prove he handled the bottle and unattended glass during the window. Remaining alternatives: Brie DeVivre, Anya Tique, Chip Patina and Barb Dwyer (6 each), with direct glass opportunity, actual cupboard access, band expertise and concealed surveillance interruption respectively. Clean flavoring is not an alibi against adding poison separately; multiple staff keys broaden cupboard access. The setting and interlocking money/ownership/service conflicts are coherent, and some occupational voices are memorable. Distinctness suffers because most of 30 people confess a hidden professional compromise, remove or revise a document, then repair the record and make a witty rueful defense. Too many simultaneous donor coercions and almost universal completed corrections make the ensemble feel procedurally arranged. Dates are internally confusing: an October 29 pre-gala proof accompanies an October 30 treatment sheet without a plainly stated gala date; I treated those as supplied story dates rather than importing today's date. Evidence is thorough on excluding proposed mechanisms, substantially thinner on who physically exploited the confirmed mechanism. Hugh is legible at the intended final round, though a reader demanding affirmative opportunity evidence could reasonably retain the alternatives.
